88631.title: Dashboard tiles load quickly and one slow tile does not hold up the others
88631.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in the busiest location (workplace) you can reach: the one with the most invoices and clocked time, so every tile has real work to do.
  3. You have a stopwatch or a phone timer ready.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: on the Dashboard, Sales by Customer (Last 12 Months) and Technician Utilization show figures; pick the location where they are largest. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
88631.custom_steps:
1. Click Work Orders in the top menu so you start away from the Dashboard.
  2. Start the stopwatch and click Dashboard in the top menu.
  3. Stop the stopwatch when all six tiles (Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization, Sales by Customer, At Risk Customers) show a figure.
  4. Write down the time.
  5. On each of the four top tiles and on Sales by Customer, click the range pill and choose Last 12 Months.
  6. Watch the tiles while each one reloads and note whether any tile stays blank or waits for another tile.
  7. Repeat steps 1 to 4 two more times and write down each time.
88631.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Each time, all six tiles show their figures in about one second. A load that clearly takes several seconds, again and again, is reported.
  • The tiles fill in on their own: no tile waits for another tile before it shows its figure.
  • This part cannot be checked by hand: the measured targets (95 of every 100 first loads within 1 second, each tile's server time within 250 ms, no single query over 500 ms, and a 2-second cut-off that fails only the slow tile). Write "targets not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see.
  • Making one tile slow or fail on purpose is not possible by hand. Write "slow-tile cut-off not checked by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; Dashboard v1 Technical Implementation Plan (sources/Dashboard-v1-Technical-Implementation-Plan.md, 2026-09-16), NFR-001, read in full 7 Oct 2026. The tech plan informs and never overrules the PRD; Dashboard v1 PRD Confluence 788430850 v42 (read 7 Oct 2026) states no speed target.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • Tech plan NFR-001: “No dashboard query may exceed 500 ms; anything above is treated as a defect and alerted. Per-tile server time targets p95 ≤ 250 ms; the six-tile first load targets p95 ≤ 1 s (a slight overrun is acceptable). Every dashboard statement carries a 2 s `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` circuit breaker, and a query that trips it fails only its own tile (FR-021)”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

88643.title: At Risk Customers counts the right customers for the chosen days
88643.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a location (workplace) with several months of invoice history (many customers, invoices going back more than a year). At Risk needs old invoices, which cannot be back-dated by hand.
  3. Customer W: in the At Risk table (window 120 Days), a customer with Lifetime Invoices 2 or more, whose newest invoice you will make and then undo. You have written down W's Last Invoice Date.
  4. Customer X: a customer whose only invoice is more than 12 months old (Lifetime Invoices 1, so Revenue (12 Mo) is $0.00).
  5. Customer Y: a customer with 2 or more invoices, all more than 12 months old.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: the At Risk Customers tile on 120 Days shows a number above 0, and View details lists customers with Last Invoice Dates spread over the last months. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
  • For 3: Dashboard > At Risk Customers on 120 Days > View details: the table shows Customer, Last Invoice Date, Lifetime Invoices and Revenue (12 Mo).
  • For 4 and 5: Customers > the customer > Invoices tab (turn Open only off) shows each invoice's date.
88643.custom_steps:
1. On the At Risk Customers tile click the window pill and choose 120 Days. Write down the headline and count the table rows.
  2. Look for customer X in the table.
  3. Look for customer Y in the table.
  4. Read down the table and check every row: Lifetime Invoices is 2 or more, or Revenue (12 Mo) is above $0.00.
  5. Window edge: on the window pill try each of 30, 60, 90, 120 and 180 Days, and look for a customer whose Last Invoice Date is exactly that many days before today (count calendar days, e.g. Jun 9, 2026 to Oct 7, 2026 = 120 days) and one at one day fewer. If the Create Invoice step on a work order lets you choose the invoice date, you may make such invoices instead.
  6. Make a new invoice today for customer W: Work Orders > Create Work Order > W and its asset > Save; in New Line one labor line (e.g. Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1), tick Line Approved > Save & Close; Story > Update; Complete (finish any Missing Details window); Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice (close the New Customer Payment window without paying).
  7. Click Dashboard, set the window to 120 Days and write down the headline. Look for W in the table.
  8. Click Work Orders, open the work order you just invoiced, Finance tab > the invoice's three dots > Reverse > confirm.
  9. Click Dashboard, set the window to 120 Days, write down the headline and find W's row.
88643.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The headline is a plain number (e.g. 12, no words, no dollar sign) and equals the number of rows in the table.
  • Customer X (one invoice, $0.00 revenue in the last 12 months) is not listed. Customer Y (2 or more invoices, $0.00 recent revenue) is listed.
  • Every listed customer has Lifetime Invoices of 2 or more, or Revenue (12 Mo) above $0.00.
  • Window edge: a customer whose newest invoice is exactly the chosen number of days old is listed, and one at one day fewer is not. If no such pair exists and invoice dates cannot be chosen, write "window edge not reachable by hand" in the result comment.
  • After invoicing W today, W leaves the list and the headline drops by 1 (e.g. 12 to 11).
  • After reversing that new invoice, W is back with its earlier Last Invoice Date and the headline returns to the step 1 figure: the undone invoice is ignored when deciding W's newest invoice.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9577 (S5); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S5 (S5-R15, S5-R7), S3 (S3-E2). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 09_AtRisk_After (table: Customer, Last Invoice Date, Lifetime Invoices, Revenue (12 Mo)), 09_AtRisk_Window.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R15: “Two parts of the at-risk definition are fixed here so the count cannot be read two ways. "Some revenue in the last twelve months" means revenue greater than $0.00 over the trailing twelve months, measured the way the Revenue tile measures revenue: invoice subtotals before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. A customer whose twelve-month revenue is exactly $0.00, or is negative because credits exceeded sales, does not satisfy this part of the test, though they can still qualify on the two-or-more-lifetime-invoices part. "At least the selected number of days old" is counted in whole calendar days in the selected workplace's timezone, from the date of the customer's most recent invoice to the current date. The count therefore changes at the shop's own midnight and is stable through the shop's working day, and two people viewing the same workplace from different places see the same number.”
  • S5-R7: “The At Risk Customers tile headline is the count of at-risk customers for the selected inactivity window, shown as a plain number.”
  • S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

  2. You are in a location (workplace) with several months of invoice history (many customers, invoices going back more than a year). At Risk needs old invoices, which cannot be back-dated by hand.
  3. You have written down the location's time zone.
  4. You have a second device (a second computer or a phone) whose clock is set to a time zone far from the location's (e.g. 8 or more hours apart), signed in as the same or another user with the Reports permission and the same location selected.
  5. The At Risk Customers table is open (Dashboard > View details under the At Risk Customers tile); it shows Customer, Last Invoice Date, Lifetime Invoices and Revenue (12 Mo).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: the At Risk Customers tile on 120 Days shows a number above 0, and View details lists customers with Last Invoice Dates spread over the last months. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
  • For 3: profile icon > Settings > Locations: the Timezone column shows it.
  • For 4: on the second device, sign in the same way (For 1) and change location as in For 2.
88644.custom_steps:
1. On your main device, set the At Risk window pill to 30 Days and write down the headline. Repeat for 60, 90, 120 and 180 Days.
  2. On the second device open Dashboard and read the At Risk headline for the same five windows.
  3. In the table on the main device pick one customer and count the calendar days from their Last Invoice Date to today's date at the location (not your own date).
  4. Read the headline again at the end of the shop's working day for the same windows, without making or undoing any invoice in between.
  5. If your working hours reach the location's midnight, read the headline a few minutes before and a few minutes after midnight at the location.
88644.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Both devices show the same At Risk count for every window, even though their clocks are in different time zones.
  • The day count uses the location's date: a customer is listed only when the days from their Last Invoice Date to the location's today are at least the chosen window.
  • The count does not change during the shop's working day (morning and evening readings match).
  • Across the location's midnight the count may change, and only then. If you cannot be working at the location's midnight, write "midnight change not checked by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9577 (S5); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S5 (S5-R15). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 09_AtRisk_After, 09_AtRisk_Window.

A customer whose twelve-month revenue is exactly $0.00, or is negative because credits exceeded sales, does not satisfy this part of the test, though they can still qualify on the two-or-more-lifetime-invoices part. "At least the selected number of days old" is counted in whole calendar days in the selected workplace's timezone, from the date of the customer's most recent invoice to the current date. 88645.title: At Risk trend line has twelve monthly points and the last equals the count
88645.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a location (workplace) with several months of invoice history (many customers, invoices going back more than a year). At Risk needs old invoices, which cannot be back-dated by hand.
  3. Customer V: with the At Risk Customers window on 120 Days, an at-risk customer whose newest invoice is from 2 to 6 months ago and who also has an older invoice. You have written down both invoice dates.
  4. Your role can reverse an invoice (Admin can).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: the At Risk Customers tile on 120 Days shows a number above 0, and View details lists customers with Last Invoice Dates spread over the last months. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
  • For 3: Dashboard > At Risk Customers window pill > 120 Days > View details; invoice dates: Customers > V > Invoices tab (turn Open only off).
88645.custom_steps:
1. Take a screenshot of the At Risk Customers tile.
  2. Count the points on the trend line, from left to right.
  3. Hover over each point and write down the month and the value it shows. If the line shows no values on hover, compare heights only.
  4. Compare the last (right-most) point with the headline.
  5. Click Work Orders, open V's newest invoiced work order, Finance tab > the invoice's three dots > Reverse > confirm. (If Reverse is not offered because the invoice is paid, first reverse its payment on Customers > V > Payments.)
  6. Click Dashboard, set the window to 120 Days, take a second screenshot and repeat steps 2 to 4.
88645.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The trend line has twelve points, one per month, for the last twelve months.
  • The right-most point equals the headline (e.g. both 12).
  • After reversing V's newest invoice, one or more of the earlier points change, not only the last one: every point is worked out again from today's data rather than kept from the past.
  • If the points show no values on hover, judge from the two screenshots and write "point values not checked by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9577 (S5); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S5 (S5-R13). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 01_Opens_After, 09_AtRisk_After.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R13: “The At Risk Customers sparkline shows the at-risk count over the trailing twelve months as twelve monthly points. Each historical point is the at-risk count as of the last day of that month in the workplace's timezone, using the inactivity window the tile currently shows. The twelfth point is computed as of now, rather than as of a month end that has not happened yet, so it always equals the headline. Every point is recomputed from current data, so a later void changes the past points: recording the count as it stood at the time would contradict S3-E2, which excludes a voided invoice even when deciding a customer's most recent invoice.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

88647.title: Trend line splits the range by day, week, month or quarter correctly
88647.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a location (workplace) with more than two years of invoices, so Revenue has a value in every period.
  3. You know how to set a custom range on the Revenue tile: click its range pill, click a start day and an end day in the calendar, check the "Range: N days" readout at the bottom, then click Apply.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: the Revenue tile shows an amount above $0.00 on Last Year and on This Year; then set the pill back to its default (the dashboard remembers your choices). If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
88647.custom_steps:
1. On Revenue set a custom range of exactly 31 days (readout "Range: 31 days"). Hover along the trend line (or count the points) and write down how many points there are and the date each shows.
  2. Set a range of exactly 32 days and do the same.
  3. Set ranges of exactly 182 days and then 183 days and do the same.
  4. Set ranges of exactly 731 days and then 732 days and do the same.
  5. On the 31-day range hover one point and write down its date and value. Open Reports > Sales, set the Date to that single day, and write down the Totals row Subtotal.
  6. On the Technician Utilization tile set a custom range that includes a day on which nobody clocked time (check Reports > Timesheet Activities, e.g. a Sunday) between days that do have clocked time. Look at the trend line around that day.
  7. On the Technician Utilization tile set a custom range in which only one day has clocked time (e.g. a single working day). Look at where the trend line would be.
88647.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • 31 days: one point per day (31 points). 32 days: one point per week.
  • 182 days: one point per week. 183 days: one point per month.
  • 731 days: one point per month. 732 days: one point per quarter.
  • The hovered day's value equals the Sales report total for that single day.
  • The day with no clocked time leaves a gap in the line: the line is not joined across it and does not drop to zero.
  • With only one day that has a value, no line is drawn. In its place the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder: a light grey dashed outline with rounded corners, no fill and a grey line-chart icon in the middle, the same height as a trend line. The headline still shows its figure.
  • If the trend line shows no dates or values on hover, count the points (zoom the browser in if needed) and write "values not checked by hand" in the result comment for the value check.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S4 (S4-R11, S4-R12). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 03_Range_After (calendar, presets, "Range: N days" readout, Apply). Design canvas row 15 (15_Empty_Design, approved 2026-10-07, to build) shows the empty-chart placeholder.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).”
  • S4-R12: “A tile shows the empty-chart placeholder in place of its sparkline when fewer than two points in the selected range have a value.”

88648.title: Each tile equals its report on every one of the nine date ranges
88648.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a location (workplace) with more than two years of invoices and clocked time, so every range has figures.
  3. You have a grid to fill in: five tiles (Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization, Sales by Customer) by nine ranges (Last 12 Months, This Year, Last Year, This Quarter, Last Quarter, This Month, Last Month, This Week, Last Week): 45 tile figures and 45 report figures.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: Revenue and Technician Efficiency show figures on Last Year and on This Year; then set the pill back to its default (the dashboard remembers your choices). If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
88648.custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu.
  2. On the Revenue tile click the range pill and choose Last 12 Months. Write down the figure.
  3. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue". Check the report's Date control covers the same dates (Last 12 Months runs from the 1st of the month eleven months back to today, e.g. on Oct 7, 2026: Nov 1, 2025 to Oct 7, 2026). Write down the Totals row Subtotal.
  4. Go back to the Dashboard and repeat steps 2 and 3 for the other eight ranges.
  5. Do the same on Billing Efficiency and compare it with the Totals row Billing Efficiency on Service Advisor Analysis (no advisor chosen).
  6. Do the same on Technician Efficiency and compare it with the report's Invoiced tab: add up the Invoiced Tech Hrs column and the Clocked Hrs column for all technicians and work out Invoiced / Clocked x 100 (e.g. 377.58 / 858.45 x 100 = 43.98%).
  7. Do the same on Technician Utilization and compare it with the report's Summary row Utilization % (Technician: All technicians).
  8. Do the same on Sales by Customer and compare it with the number of customer rows on the Sales By Customer report.
88648.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • For each of the nine ranges, Revenue equals the Sales report's Totals row Subtotal.
  • For each range, Billing Efficiency equals the Service Advisor Analysis Totals row Billing Efficiency.
  • For each range, Technician Efficiency equals your Invoiced / Clocked figure from the report's Invoiced tab.
  • For each range, Technician Utilization equals the Technician Utilization Summary row Utilization %.
  • For each range, the Sales by Customer count equals the number of customers on the Sales By Customer report.
  • Each report covers exactly the same dates as its tile for every range, including Last 12 Months. All 45 pairs match.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9579 (S7), story SV-9582 (S10); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R1, context note), S7 (S7-R2), S10 (S10-R8). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 02_Last12_After, 03_Range_After, 10_sales_After, 11_service-advisor-analysis_After, 12_technician-efficiency_After, 13_technician-utilization_After.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S7-R2: “The date-range control offers, in this order: Last 12 Months, This Year, Last Year, This Quarter, Last Quarter, This Month, Last Month, This Week, Last Week.”
  • S10-R8: “"Last 12 months" covers the same window on every tile and in every report the dashboard links to: from the first day of the month eleven months before the current month, through today, in the workplace's timezone. Example: on October 5, 2026 it covers November 1, 2025 to October 5, 2026.”
  • S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

  6. Back on the Dashboard, set Technician Efficiency to Last 12 Months, click View details, and in the Technician filter keep only two technicians (any two).
  7. Hover last month's point and write down each technician's percentage.
  8. Click Reports > Technician Efficiency, Invoiced tab, Date: Last month, and write down those two technicians' Efficiency.
  9. Repeat steps 6 to 8 on Technician Utilization, comparing with the Technician Utilization report with the same two technicians chosen in its Technician filter.
  10. On Reports > Advisor Analysis keep the same advisor chosen, set the Date control to This year, and hover last month's point on the chart above the table.
  11. On the Dashboard set Billing Efficiency to This Year with the same advisor chosen and hover last month's point.
88649.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Billing Efficiency chart filtered to one advisor shows only that advisor's line, and last month's point equals the report filtered to the same advisor for last month (percentage and ELR, after rounding).
  • The Technician Efficiency chart filtered to two technicians shows only their lines, and each one's last-month point equals the report's Efficiency for that technician.
  • The Technician Utilization chart filtered the same way matches the Technician Utilization report for those technicians.
  • The chart on the Advisor Analysis report, under the report's own advisor and date filters, shows the same last-month value as the report and as the Dashboard chart with the same advisor.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. Preconditions

  3. You run this case before the last day of the month, so This Month is not finished yet.
  4. If a total differs only in the last decimal place (0.01) because rows are rounded, mark the case Blocked and write both numbers in the comment: the specification does not cover rounding of row sums.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
88650.custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu. The four top tiles open on This Month.
  2. On Technician Efficiency write down the headline and the line under it (e.g. 377.58 Invoiced Tech Hrs / 858.45 Clocked).
  3. Click View details on Technician Efficiency. Page through the table and add up the Clocked Hrs column and the Invoiced Tech Hrs column.
  4. Work out Invoiced / Clocked x 100 from your sums.
  5. On Technician Utilization click View details. Add up WO Hours, Internal Hours and Total Hours.
  6. On Billing Efficiency click View details. Add up Worked Hours and Invoiced Hrs.
  7. On Revenue click View details. Hover each bar of the chart and add up the values.
  8. Look at the right-hand end of each tile's trend line.
88650.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Technician Efficiency: the Clocked Hrs sum equals the Clocked figure, the Invoiced Tech Hrs sum equals the Invoiced Tech Hrs figure, and your Invoiced / Clocked x 100 equals the headline.
  • Technician Utilization: the WO Hours sum equals the WO Hrs figure, the Total Hours sum equals the Clocked figure, and WO Hours + Internal Hours = Total Hours.
  • Billing Efficiency: the Worked Hours sum equals the Clocked figure and the Invoiced Hrs sum equals the Invoiced figure.
  • Revenue: the chart's bars add up to the headline.
  • The chart and table cover the same range as the tile (This Month), and no point or row contradicts the tile.
  • Each trend line stops at today: there are no points for the days of the month still to come, so the line and the headline cover the same part of the month.
